label: input token n (fed-back copy of n, plus weak at t=0)
explanation: Token detector for the input letter n. It fires on every copy-phase step whose input is n (the model feeding back an n it just output): dev precision 1.0, 95% of activation mass, typical activation 0.6-1.0 of max. The strongest cases are the first n of an n n pair in the copy phase (about 1.0), and the second n of the pair is a little weaker (about 0.8). It also fires weakly (about 0.13) when n is the very first original token (t=0), but almost never on n at later original-phase positions, and never at the delimiter. What it misses is small weak activity (about 0.1-0.17) on other inputs, mostly x, h or i, often just before an n in the copy phase. This is 1.6% of activation mass.

issues: Claims check out on the test split. Copy-phase n gives precision 1.0 and 95.3% of activation mass. n at t=0 gives precision 1.0, but those steps fall only in the lowest activation quartile, so they are weak (consistent with ~0.13). n at original positions t>0 has precision 0.015, so it is effectively silent there. The delimiter is never active.

The n n pair claim holds. The first n of a copy-phase pair (rel_tok(1)==n) sits mostly in the top activation quartile (coverage 0.078 there against 0.008, 0.002 and ~0 in the lower ones). The second n (prev_tok==n) is spread across quartiles 2-4 at ~0.026-0.029 each, so it is weaker.

The misses on the test split are 8115 steps holding 1.5% of activation mass, all in the lowest activation quartile (~0.11-0.15). They are spread over x, h, g, c and others, usually the input just before an n in the copy phase, plus a few n at t=1. There are no false positives.

Adding the step whose output is n (out_tok==n) drops precision to 0.57, F1 0.718. Adding t==1 drops precision to 0.875, F1 0.906. Neither beats the original predicate, so no systematic gap remains beyond weak noise.
